- Stakeholders we surfaced:
  - Economic buyer: Victor Lin, CFO (decision authority on budget)
  - Procurement: procurement@acme.com (procurement lead: Sarah Patel)
  - Security: Alice Zhang (alice.zhang@acme.com) - needs SOC2 / network diagram review

Key decision criteria you called out: latency at scale, predictable unit cost, and compliance attestations.

Ask from our side: can you confirm the procurement and legal review timeline? You mentioned a 4–8 week procurement window but asked whether we can accommodate an SLA and a one-time implementation credit for a faster rollout.

Attached is the draft_pricing.xlsx and an initial SOW (SOW_Acme_v1.pdf) for budget/PO planning.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll map the procurement steps and request a small buying-process exception if needed (discount/SLA).
2) Neha (cc’d) will coordinate the SOC2 and security questionnaire exchange with Alice.
3) Can you share the preferred PO process and contract reviewers?

Will follow up with a mutual action plan once we hear back from procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>

Date: 2026-11-30T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — next steps / stakeholder map

Marissa — great demo, appreciated the clear perf numbers. A few notes from our side:

- Procurement process: Acme requires a PO + signed agreement. Our procurement lead typically runs a 30–60 day review with legal for commercial terms, and security does an independent questionnaire review in parallel.
- Security: Alice needs SOC 2 Type II report and a network diagram. She’ll schedule a short deep-dive next week.
- Decision criteria: total cost of ownership (first year + run rate), latency SLA, and data handling controls.

On the SLA/discount ask: I can push for a shortened legal review if we have an approved commercial term set (and a committed AD/PO). For budget purposes, can you confirm the license/seat pricing and what a first-year discount would look like? Also, we need clarity on remediation/credits for SLA misses — procurement will expect a credit schedule.

If you can send a mutual action plan (dates, deliverables) we’ll align internal stakeholders this week.

Thanks,
John
Head of Platform, Acme Corp
john.doe@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T08:37:00-08:00
Subject: FW: Acme — procurement & SLA ask — request for buying-process exception (discount + SLA credit schedule)

Aditya — looping you in. Acme looks strategically important (fast-growing, likely $800k–1.2M ARR in year 1 if we land their platform scope). Procurement is likely to insist on: PO + signed agreement, SOC2 evidence, and a formal SLA credit schedule. They’ve asked whether we can:

- Offer a 25% first-year discount to meet budget targets, and
- Commit to a 99.9% latency SLA with defined credits for misses (procurement wants this codified in the MSA)

They also asked for a shortened legal review if commercial terms are pre-approved. Given the timeline, I’m requesting a buying-process exception to approve a one-time commercial concession (discount + SLA credits) and to allow legal to prioritize the redline within 10 business days.

Justification: strategic logo, referenceability, and expected expansion. Proposed guardrails: discount limited to first 12 months, renewal at standard list thereafter; SLA credit cap at 25% of monthly invoice; require legal to sign off on MSA redline (we’ll push 20% discount instead of 25% if legal requests tighter limits).

Attachments: SOW_Acme_v1.pdf, draft_pricing.xlsx.

Please approve or advise next steps — need an internal decision so I can give procurement a firm answer by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: Acme — procurement & SLA ask — request for buying-process exception (discount + SLA credit schedule)

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary and the business case. I approve a bounded exception with the following conditions:

1) Commercial: approve up to 20% first-year discount (not to exceed 20% without VP-level approval).
2) SLA: we can agree to a 99.9% latency SLA with a credit schedule capped at 25% of the monthly invoice. Credits are retrospective and triggered after validated incidents; legal must draft the exact credit language.
3) Term guardrails: discount applies only for the first 12 months; renewal will revert to list pricing unless a renewal discount is re-approved.
4) Legal: require in-parallel priority review; do not sign any MSA redline that increases risk exposure (especially indemnity/limit-of-liability changes).

Please route the proposed MSA redline to Legal (cc: neha_kapoor) and create a HubSpot note with the approved exception. I’ll notify finance to prepare the renewal/discount codes for billing.

Deal approved under exception: ACME-2026-Q4-037. Keep me posted if procurement pushes harder.

Aditya
Head of Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
